depth: The monocular depth map captures a top-down view of a salon interior where a seated person's foil-covered head is directly below and in front of the standing camera wearer at about 3–5 metres, far and out of reach (brightest background), flanked on the left out of arm's reach (3–5 metres) by a tray table holding a dye bowl, foil, and a towel, and an empty salon chair at 3–5 metres. Before the distant seated client and within arm's reach at roughly 0.5–1.2 metres are wall mirrors, drawer cabinets, and in frame 3 a second worker crouching on the right about 3–5 metres away near the client's extended foot and blue foot-bath basin, with the client and workers facing toward or upward relative to the camera wearer and looking up. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's black-gloved right arm enters the background in frames 4 and 5 at 3–5 metres (pure white), partially occluding the client's head and sitting roughly 3–5 metres to the right of the left-hand dye bowl. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the background head, distant tray and chair armrests, and nearby wall cabinets into distinct distance layers despite complex visual clutter. However, the map is unreliable on the wall mirrors, where virtual reflections of the salon chair, foot basin, and opposite room are rendered with false nearby depth (0.5–1.2 metres) instead of the flat planar surface of the mirror glass within reach at ~0.6 metres.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture most of the salon layout, detecting objects only in frames 1, 3, and 4 while leaving frames 2 and 5, as well as all background mirrors, cabinets, trays, and chairs, completely unsegmented. In frame 1, it detects the seated client's head in the lower-right background (~3–5 metres from the camera wearer, out of arm's reach) but misclassifies the foil-wrapped hair as a 'couch' while labeling only a tiny sliver of the client's lower-right leg/foot at ~3–5 metres as 'person'. In frame 3, as the camera turns slightly right, the second worker crouching at ~3–5 metres on the upper-right facing the client's outstretched foot (out of that worker's arm's reach, ~3–5 metres from the client's torso) is misclassified as a 'dog', while the client and background tools are missed entirely. In frame 4, the map correctly segments the combined silhouette of the camera wearer's reaching right arm (3–5 metres) and the client's occluded head (3–5 metres) as a single 'person' mask, though it merges the two individuals together and misses the camera wearer's left hand by the dye bowl. While the mask boundary in frame 4 sharply isolates the background human silhouette from the dark floor and chair foreground, the segmentation map is highly unreliable due to severe top-down perspective distortion, heavy occlusion by hair foils and capes, and false or merged class labels.
pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame sequence, detecting a single yellow body skeleton only in the upper-right quadrant of frame 3 and nothing in frames 1, 2, 4, or 5. In frame 3, this skeleton localizes the second person crouching on the floor about 3–5 metres to the right-front of the camera wearer and roughly 3–5 metres in front of the seated client, oriented toward the lower-left where the client's lower legs extend into a foot basin out of that person's arm's reach. The plotted head, torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, and knee keypoints show this crouching person angled downward toward the client's foot and facing toward the camera wearer. Compared to the dark clothing and awkward top-down angle in the RGB strip, the skeleton in frame 3 clarifies the compact, bent-knee posture and arm reach of the crouching worker. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for this steeply angled egocentric scene, completely missing the seated client directly below the camera (3–5 metres, out of reach and occluded by hair foils and a cape), failing to track the crouching worker when partially cut off by the frame edge in other frames, and detecting no magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's black-gloved hands reaching at 3–5 metres in frames 1 through 5.
